argument_summary: The certification claim should be narrowed rather than treated as clean compliance. On the admissible record, aggregate readiness is supportable because the release clears launch readiness by 2.0 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring residual risk through deployment. The same record also shows a 1.2 percentage-point miss in a named launch use case tied to two customer commitments, an open legal disclosure question, and policy text that makes those facts material. The defensible packet position is therefore that certification can be presented only with an explicit caveat that the evidentiary and policy basis is contested, not that the issue is immaterial or fully resolved.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to justify the packet position. The record can be defended on a risk-weighted basis only by distinguishing general launch readiness from unresolved policy compliance for the named segment.
claims_about_policy: The policy does not support calling this cleanly compliant on the present record. The strongest supportable reading is narrower: aggregate readiness and standard governance practice justify certification only as a caveated position while explicitly acknowledging that the named-use-case limitation appears material under policy unless it is resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Public model-card and risk-management guidance support documentation and monitoring, but they do not by themselves satisfy the specific release-policy predicate.
concessions: There is no admissible evidence that the named-use-case limitation was resolved before launch.
There is no admissible evidence of approved risk acceptance covering this segment.
The open legal ticket means the disclosure predicate remains unresolved.
The non-core 6% traffic note does not resolve materiality because the segment is named in customer commitments.
